original_question: Let C : f = 0 be a reduced plane curve in P^2 with isolated singularities. Is the freeness defect nu(C) determined solely by the degree of C together with the list of analytic types of its singularities?
target_in_paper: Conjecture 3.8 in Section 3 ('Terao’s Conjecture and some generalizations'): for a reduced plane curve C:f=0 in P^2, the invariant ν(C) is determined by the degree of C and the list of the analytic types of the isolated singularities of C. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the exact target invariant ν(C), the ambient class of objects (reduced plane curves in P^2), and the decisive input data (degree together with analytic singularity types). It is essentially a close paraphrase of the paper’s Conjecture 3.8. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
missing_details: The paper works over the complex numbers: S=C[x,y,z] and C is a curve in the complex projective plane P^2, not over an arbitrary field. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

To make the question stand alone, one should say that f∈S is a reduced homogeneous polynomial of degree d=deg f; the standing setup in Section 2 assumes d≥3. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The freeness defect ν(C) is not defined in the draft. In the paper, J_f=(f_x,f_y,f_z), I_f is the saturation of J_f with respect to m=(x,y,z), M(f)=S/J_f, N(f)=I_f/J_f=H^0_m(M(f)), and ν(C)=max_j dim_C N(f)_j. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The paper’s wording is 'the list of the analytic types of the isolated singularities of C,' i.e. the multiset of local analytic singularity types. For a reduced plane curve in P^2, the singularities are isolated, so your added phrase is compatible but somewhat redundant. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

The quantifier should be universal: the claim is meant for every reduced plane curve in this setup, with ν(C) depending only on d and those local analytic types. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))

Nearby context omitted in the draft: the paper notes immediately after Conjecture 3.8 that the conjecture is already known when r=mdr(f)≥(d−2)/2, by Theorem 2.3. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
refined_question: Let S=C[x,y,z], let f∈S be a reduced homogeneous polynomial of degree d≥3, and let C:f=0⊂P^2_C be the corresponding reduced plane curve. If J_f=(f_x,f_y,f_z), I_f is the saturation of J_f with respect to m=(x,y,z), N(f)=I_f/J_f, and ν(C)=max_j dim_C N(f)_j, is ν(C) determined by d together with the list of local analytic types of the isolated singularities of C? ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting the paper’s general reduced-plane-curve conjecture, stated explicitly as Conjecture 3.8 right after the line-arrangement version Conjecture 3.7, rather than a broader neighboring problem. Section 2 supplies the standing notation over C and the definitions of mdr(f), the Jacobian module N(f), and the freeness defect ν(C), all of which are needed to make the question fully self-contained. The sentence immediately following Conjecture 3.8 records the relevant nearby context: the conjecture is already known in the range mdr(f)≥(d−2)/2 by Theorem 2.3. ([imar.ro](https://imar.ro/journals/Revue_Mathematique/pdfs/2024/2/4.pdf))
